title: Isolation and functional characterization of human glioblastoma stem cells
protocol: Pre-mix aliquots of dissociation enzymes containing 40 mg trypsin, 20 mg hyaluronidase, and 3-5 mg kynurenic acid.
Keep the pre-mixed enzyme aliquots in -20°C dessicator until use.

Prepare human ACSF by combining 100 mL of 2M NaCl, 6.2 mL of 1M KCl, 0.5 mL of 1M MgCl₂, 0.32 mL of 155 mM NaHCO₃, 16.9 mL of 1 M Glucose, 1.0 mL of 108 mM CaCl₂, 2.0 mL of 1 M HEPES, 1.0 mL of 1X Antibiotic/antimycotic (PSF), and 72 mL ddH₂O.
Dissect and discard white matter from tumour tissue.
Snap freeze small tumour pieces by immersion in liquid nitrogen.
Place individual frozen tumour pieces in separately labelled cryovials.
Transfer the labeled cryovials to a designated box in -80°C freezer.
Place small tumour pieces in mesh cassettes and place them in 10% Formalin.
Mince remaining tumour tissue finely, ideally to a “jelly-like” consistency.
Transfer sample into a 50 mL conical tube.
Fill the tube to 20 mL with human ACSF.
Dissolve dissociation enzymes (40 mg Trypsin, 20 mg Hyaluronidase, 3-5 mg Kynurenic acid) in 10 mL of human ACSF.
Filter the solution with a .22 µm syringe filter.
If the mixture is gelatinous or sticky, add 45 μL of DNAse.
Add 10 mL of sterile glass beads into the tube for mechanical dissociation.
Nutate the mixture in a rotating incubator at 37°C for 15 – 50 minutes as needed.
Remove the mixture from the incubator when fully homogenized.
Remove dissociated tumour suspension using a 10 mL pipette and transfer to a new 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 1000 rpm.
Resuspend pellet in 20-30mL DMEM.
Filter sample through a 40 µm mesh.
Centrifuge again at 1000 rpm.
If needed, use 12 mL of Lympholyte-Mammal (Cedarlane CL5110) to improve tumour cell purity.
Resuspend tumour cells in 10 mL DMEM.
Count tumour cells using a hemocytometer to distinguish them from red blood cells or lymphocytes based on size.
Optionally, purify the sample by magnetic bead depletion against human CD31 and CD45 expressing cells.
Cryopreserve viable cells in 5% BSA, 10% DMSO in DMEM at a concentration of 1×10^6 cells/mL.
Expand primary cells for 5 passages to generate a culture of GBM stem cells.
Perform primary LDA analysis by plating dissociated GBM cells in 6 replicates into the inner 60 wells of 96-well tissue culture suspension plates using human neural stem cell media.
Use 10 cell doses, generally two-fold dilutions starting at 2000 cells and ending at 4 cells suspended in 100 μL of NS-A expansion media.
Top up the media in each well with 50 μL of NS-A expansion media after the first week of culture.
Score each well for the presence or absence of neurospheres after the second week.
Mix a bottle of basal neural stem cell media by combining 450 mL of human Neurocult NS-A Basal medium with 5 mL of 200 mM L-Glutamine and 500 μL of 7.5% BSA solution.
Store the prepared basal neural stem cell media at 4°C.

Prepare 50 mL of NS-A Expansion media by combining 44.2 mL of basal medium, 5.0 mL of 10X hormone mix, 1.0 mL of 50X B27 supplement, 2.5 μL of 200 μg/mL rhEGF, 125 μL of 4 μg/mL bFGF, and 100 μL of 1 mg/mL Heparin.

Make up the 10X hormone mix in advance by combining 100 mL of DMEM:F12, 4 mL of 0.6% Glucose, 200 mg Transferrin, 50 mg Insulin, 19.33 mg Putrescine, 200 μL of Sodium Selenite, 20 μL of Progesterone with Milli-Q water up to a total volume of 200 mL.
Aliquot the prepared 10X hormone mix and store at -20°C.
Coat Corning-Primaria tissue culture vessels with poly-L-ornithine for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the poly-L-ornithine and coat with laminin diluted in PBS at a ratio of 1:200, again at room temperature.
Thaw frozen GSCs in a 37°C water bath.
Transfer the solution into 10 mL of DMEM media and mix gently.
Centrifuge cells at 1000 rpm for 5 minutes to recover the cell pellet.
Aspirate the supernatant and gently resuspend the cell pellet in pre-warmed NS-A expansion media.
Remove laminin solution from a coated culture vessel.
Transfer the cell suspension into the vessel, using approximately 1×10^6 cells per 10 cm Primaria culture dish.
Replenish cell culture media every 2-3 days by removing half of the conditioned media and replacing it with fresh media.
Remove media from the cell culture vessel.
Add Accutase solution to coat the bottom of the vessel.
Place the vessel back into the incubator for 5 minutes.
Resuspend cells in 10 mL of DMEM media.
Spin the suspension for 5 minutes at 1000 rpm.
Split cells between 1:3 to 1:5 ratios.
Add the cells into a pre-coated Primaria vessel.
Harvest GBM cells by accutase treatment if using cultured cells.
Wash the sample twice in sterile PBS.
Resuspend the sample in a small volume of PBS for transplantation.
Anesthetize the mouse with 1-3% isoflurane in a gas chamber.
Transfer the mouse to the stereotactic headframe.
Redirect flow of isofluorane from the chamber to the stereotactic headframe.
Check that the mouse is fully anesthetized by toe pinch.
Inject 500 uL of analgesic subcutaneously into the mouse using a 5 mL syringe and 25G needle.
Clip hair to expose skin of forehead.
Apply eye gel to eyes.
Apply betadine to forehead.
Clean the skin with 70% EtOH.
Make an incision with a disposable scalpel blade at the midline on top of the skull, approximately 0.5 cm in length.
Attach a 1 mL syringe to a 21G needle.
Position the syringe directly on top of bregma where frontal and parietal bones meet.
Move the needle 1 mm down and 2 mm right for forebrain injections.
Alternatively, position the needle on top of lambda where sagittal and lambdoid sutures meet, then move 4 mm up and 2 mm to the right.
Lower the syringe to create a dent in the skull at the desired coordinates.
Remove the syringe and manually bore a hole through the skull at the marked injection site with a 21G needle.
Assemble the injection needle consisting of a Hamilton syringe and a Hamilton 26G Small Hub RN Needle.
Flush the needle 3 times with ethanol, 3 times with water, then 3 times with PBS to ensure cleanliness and prevent clogging.
Drug up the desired volume of cells with the needle and clamp onto the headframe.
Reposition the needle directly on top of the hole in the skull.
Lower the needle by 3.5 mm.
Wait 30 seconds, then raise the needle by 0.5 mm to create a small pocket in the brain.
Inject the cells slowly over 2-3 minutes.
After injection, allow the needle to remain in the brain for another 2 minutes.
Slowly draw up the needle in the headframe over 1-2 minutes.
Cover the bore hole with bone wax.
Suture and place mouse in a new clean cage that rests on a warming blanket.
Monitor the mouse directly post-surgery.
Monitor the mouse over the next three consecutive days.
Wash the Hamilton syringe 3 times in water.
